_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, margin, expense and receivables signals with Google's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Alphabet is a collection of businesses — the largest of which is Google — which we report as two segments: Google Services and Google Cloud.' 'We generate a significant portion of our revenues from advertising, and reduced spending by advertisers, a loss of partners, or new and existing technologies that block ads online and/or affect our ability to customize ads could harm our business.' 'We face intense competition.' 'As our growth rate has slowed, the cyclicality and seasonality in our business has become more pronounced and caused our operating results to fluctuate.' 'In addition, expenditures by advertisers tend to be cyclical, reflecting overall economic conditions and budgeting and buying patterns.' 'Our business is affected by seasonal fluctuations in internet usage, advertising expenditures, and underlying business trends such as traditional retail seasonality (including developments and volatility arising from COVID-19).' (FY2020 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a search and advertising company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services; CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and this 10-K names the cloud as Google's own business and its competitors in it ('Providers of enterprise cloud services, including Alibaba, Amazon, and Microsoft.'), so it is out of scope (the AVGO FY2012 and NVDA reading); ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (from 2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (from 2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels; EV (from 2020-01-01) to combustion-engine vehicles and their suppliers; CRYPTO (from 2020-10-21) to payment networks, banks and exchanges), so the watch list is empty; the competition named is a competitive field, not a theme, and stays here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -35.4%/yr (worst year FY11-FY20, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +23.0%/yr (Q4 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +23.0%/yr (FY11-FY20 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +65.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY11-FY20, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: GOOG (retrospective, 2021-02-26) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 3.71x (77.6% downside to Bear $455.33 / +21.0% upside to Bull $2463.64) | Adj composite 1.91 vs market 2.72: gap -0.81 [OVERVALUED] | +74% above the EPP floor $1,172.20 (20x FY21E $58.61) | Conservative 2-yr case: +5.3% total (+2.6%/yr) | At 34.8x FY21E the 15% hurdle price $2,693.75 sits above the BULL case; revenue +23.5% YoY in Q4 2020, forward revenues +23.5% (Q4 2020 revenue growth (no Q1 2021 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
